- If sentiment is negative (especially > -0.15) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops) and forecast is flat or rising, adjust downward to reflect momentum.  
- After a spike in price (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), forecast should not overshoot by more than 2–3% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, forecast should not be >1.5% above recent 7-day average unless confirmed by volume or news.  
- If true outcome shows sharp reversal after a forecast peak, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period to avoid lagged overreaction.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from forecast in first 5 days, adjust future forecast downward by 0.5–1% per day to reflect volatility.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple negative values (e.g., 3+ in last 7 days), forecast should be capped at 1–2% below recent 14-day average.
